## How a recommendation is made

```
issue labels ──► lang/<key> + job/<key>        (hatsu:classify writes them)
repo kind/role + issue labels + jobs ──► domain (first matching rule wins)
(job, domain, language) ──► routing cell       (winner + runner-up, each an ALIAS)
alias ──► provider · model family · surface · tier ──► the name you type
job weights + counts + domain ──► effort       (low | medium | high | max)
```

1. **Two labels decide it.** `lang/` is what the work is written in (`swift`, `kotlin`, `typescript`, `csharp`, `prose`); `job/` is the kind of work (39 keys, below). `hatsu:classify` applies them; `direct` only reads them.
2. **The domain is derived, never labelled** — from the repository's kind and role, the issue's labels and its jobs ([rules](#which-domain-am-i-in)).
3. **One cell per (job, language), three picks.** Every cell names a *winner* — the **primary**, the cost-aligned best — and a *runner-up* — the **fallback**, on another provider or surface; the **recommended** (cost-agnostic) pick follows by rule ([the three picks](#primary-fallback-recommended--the-three-picks)). A language column only exists in the data where that language is routed differently; otherwise the shared `*` cell applies (and `prose` always reads `*`).
4. **An alias is stable; a version is not.** The alias names a provider, a model line, a model family, the Hatsu surface it runs on and its tier. The name you type comes from `nen/workflow.json` → `models.<modelsKey>.<tier>` (`claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `antigravity`); the newest version and the effort dial are read live when `direct` runs, with the dated snapshot below as the fallback.
5. **No `job/` label, no recommendation** — `emptyAxis.job`: *undirectable: the job axis is empty -- one line in the report, no cell, no effort, no mismatch asked; the caller (build) continues on its own session*

*This walkthrough is a hand-written summary; every section below it is rendered from the data.*

## Primary, fallback, recommended — the three picks

> The three picks every cell yields, and what each is for (the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-05, docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-10-05 -- the registry rebalance). The cell keys stay `winner` and `runnerUp` because nen direct resolve reads those; this block fixes their meaning. One more word of the verb's is fixed here: `mismatch.compares[].recommended` in the resolve document is the PRIMARY's value (the verb's word predates the three picks); its rename is zheref/nen#389.

| Pick | What it is | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| **primary** | the cell's `winner`: the cost-aligned best -- the lowest tier that loses nothing material on the job (ECON-3). It is what nen direct resolve reports as the winner, what the restart line names and what build compares the session against first. | the cell's `winner`, `nen direct resolve`'s winner |
| **fallback** | the cell's `runnerUp`: the cost-aligned second best on a DIFFERENT provider or surface (`fallbackRule`), so the work can move when one pool's funds or credits run out. A reviewer alias in that position resolves through its `also`. AT THE AGGREGATE (several pairs), the verb's runner-up is the fallback when it sits in another pool than the primary; when it shares the primary's pool, the fallback is the highest-precedence alias in another pool among the pairs' winners and runner-ups, named beside the verb's runner-up with the word `aggregate` -- derived by the reader from the resolve document until the verb applies the rule (zheref/nen#389). | the cell's `runnerUp`, the verb's runner-up |
| **recommended** | the cost-agnostic best: what to run when price is no object | aliases.<primary>.escalation when the resolve's highest job weight is 4 OR its effort level is max, and that escalation is not null; otherwise the primary itself |

`picks.fallbackRule`: *for every cell: the actionable fallback's provider differs from the primary's, or its surface does. Checked by scripts/direct_matrix_doc.sh --self-test over every cell; the nen direct registry check is zheref/nen#389.*

What each primary escalates to when the rule fires:

| Primary | Recommended on a weight-4 job or a `max` effort |
|---|---|
| 🟠 `fable` · Claude Code | itself — nothing above it |
| 🟢 `astra` · Codex | itself — nothing above it |
| 🟠 `opus` · Claude Code | 🟠 `fable` · Claude Code |
| 🟢 `sol` · Codex | 🟢 `astra` · Codex |
| 🔵 `pro` · Antigravity | itself — nothing above it |
| ⚫ `grok` · Cursor | itself — nothing above it |
| 🟠 `sonnet` · Claude Code | 🟠 `opus` · Claude Code |
| 🟢 `terra` · Codex | 🟢 `sol` · Codex |
| 🔵 `flash` · Antigravity | 🔵 `pro` · Antigravity |
| ⚫ `composer` · Cursor | ⚫ `grok` · Cursor |

`picks.tiers`: *the alias's `tier` is one of nen/workflow.json -> models' four keys -- frontier, deep, fast, economy -- and the primaries live on deep and fast: Opus, Sol, Grok and Pro are the deep tier; Sonnet, Terra, Composer and Flash the fast tier; Fable and Astra the frontier tier, reached only as `recommended`. No alias names the economy tier: it is the watcher and formatter roles' (WORKFLOW section models), never a pick.*

**Companion jobs** (`companion: true` in the taxonomy): `review`, `delivery-ops`. Jobs that never stand alone on an issue because they are phases of the effort that carries them -- flagged `companion: true` in contracts/classify.taxonomy.json (review, delivery-ops). THE VERB KEEPS DECIDING: beside any non-companion job, `--job` carries ONLY the non-companion jobs, and that call's aggregate, effort, picks, compare and --record are the verdict; a second `nen direct resolve` over the companion jobs alone reports them as companion rows -- that work runs on the SESSION'S surface (the surface the effort runs on, which is where hanten raises its reviewers: hanten sections 4 and 7) at models.roles.<role> (review -> reviewer, delivery-ops -> worker; the tier beside a lower-tier session is zheref/hatsu#222, open, not ruled here). An issue carrying ONLY companion jobs (review alone, review + delivery-ops, a hotfix backport) is one call over them, no strike: its own cells direct it. The companion rows never change the primary, the fallback, the effort or the compare. A `companion` flag honoured by the verb itself (one call, the rows marked) is zheref/nen#389.

| Companion job | Runs on the primary's surface at |
|---|---|
| `review` | `models.roles.reviewer` → tier `deep` |
| `delivery-ops` | `models.roles.worker` → tier `fast` |

## Which domain am I in?

Rules are checked in `order`; **the first match wins** (`domains.rule`).

| # | Domain | When |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **AI governance** (`aigov`) | nen repo classify reports kind process, or role canon |
| 2 | **Reusable library** (`library`) | nen repo classify reports kind library |
| 3 | **Cross-platform parity** (`parity`) | the issue carries job/parity, the marker job -- reached only in a product repository: rows 1 and 2 (a process or library repository) win first and keep their own table |
| 4 | **Maintenance & operations** (`maintenance`) | the issue carries the repository's bug kind label (a label named bug, or <ns>:bug), or it carries at least one job and every job it carries lists only maintenance phases |
| 5 | **Feature development** (`feature`) | otherwise |

`domains.fallback`: *A job with no phase in the derived domain routes on the first domain it does list, in this order: the derived domain, then maintenance, feature, library, aigov, parity. Every job lists at least one domain, so the fallback always ends; the report names the substitution.*

## Job × language — one matrix per domain

The registry's routing is keyed **(job, domain, language)** — 5 tables, one per domain, each varying by language. Pick your domain, find your job's row, read your language's column. Each cell is that pair's **winner**, then its runner-up, then the interactive tool the source prefers where it names one. A **bold** winner is routed for that language specifically, unlike the shared cell. A row in *↪ italics* has no phase in this domain and borrows the route of the domain named — you meet it when the issue's other jobs put it in this domain. `prose` always reads the shared cell.

## How hard — the effort rule

**score = the max job weight**, plus one for each of:

- three or more jobs
- two or more code languages (prose does not count)
- the derived domain is aigov

| Score | Effort |
|---|---|
| ≤ 2 | **low** |
| 3 | **medium** |
| 4 | **high** |
| ≥ 5 | **max** |

Job weights:

| Weight | Jobs |
|---|---|
| 4 | `requirements`, `architecture`, `api-design`, `security` |
| 3 | `discovery`, `analysis`, `orchestration`, `ux`, `integration`, `accessibility`, `integration-tests`, `ui-automation`, `performance`, `review`, `release`, `observability`, `bug-fix`, `migration`, `deprecation`, `prose-authoring`, `schema`, `evals`, `drift-review`, `parity` |
| 2 | `backlog`, `ui`, `implementation`, `unit-tests`, `ci-cd`, `triage`, `refactor`, `upgrades`, `machinery`, `documentation`, `adapters`, `onboarding`, `provisioning`, `delivery-ops` |
| 1 | `mechanical-edit` |

How each surface spells the level (`effort.surfaceMap`):

| Level | Claude Code | Codex | Cursor | Antigravity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| low | `low` | `low` | `low` | `low` |
| medium | `medium` | `medium` | `medium` | `medium` |
| high | `high` | `high` | `high` | `high` |
| max | `max` | `max` | `xhigh` | `high` |

`effort.surfaceMap.$collapsed`: *antigravity has no top setting: max maps to high there, said in the report; a session at high on antigravity MATCHES a recommended max because effort is compared in dial space (see mismatch). Codex gained max (and ultra) and Cursor's ids carry -xhigh, read live on 2026-10-05, so neither collapses any more; a dial the live read lists that this map lacks is quoted beside the line, never typed into it.*

## Several jobs or languages on one issue

Every (job, language) pair gets its own cell; one recommendation comes out. The rule, as `aggregation.$comment` states it:

> An issue carrying several jobs or languages resolves ONE actionable recommendation. Each (job, language) pair yields its cell. WINNER (the PRIMARY pick): count winner positions only; the alias with the most wins, ties broken by `precedence` (earlier wins). A reviewer alias (aliases.<a>.reviewer true) is never the winner: a pair it wins counts for its `also` alias. RUNNER-UP (the FALLBACK pick): the alias with the next-highest winner count among the other winning aliases, ties by `precedence`; when the winner won every pair, the most frequent runnerUp alias across the winner's pairs, a reviewer alias resolving to its `also`, ties by `precedence`. Every reviewer runnerUp in this file carries an `also`, so a runner-up always resolves to an actionable alias. Every per-pair cell is still reported so the maintainer can see where the aggregate departs from a pair. PRECEDENCE ranks the semantic alias of a tier before the execution alias of the same tier: a tie carries at least one semantic pair, and the semantic reader is the one pick the fallback cannot replace at parity (ruling of 2026-10-05); the two escalation aliases are ranked first only because nen direct registry requires every alias ranked -- no cell names one as a winner or a runner-up, so those two slots are unreachable. Companion jobs (`companions`) are kept out of the call that decides, never struck from a tally.

`precedence`, earliest first: `SEMANTIC_MAX` › `EXECUTION_MAX` › `SEMANTIC_FRONTIER` › `EXECUTION_FRONTIER` › `VISUAL_ORCHESTRATOR` › `EDITOR_FRONTIER` › `BALANCED_AUTHOR` › `EXECUTION_VALUE` › `VISUAL_FALLBACK` › `MECHANICAL_EDITOR` › `PR_QUALITY_REVIEW` › `PR_SECURITY_REVIEW`.

Where no other alias is left the verb returns no runner-up, and `direct` reports it as *fallback: none distinct* ([`direct`](../claude/skills/direct/SKILL.md) § 5). Where the verb's runner-up shares the primary's provider and surface, the aggregate fallback is the highest-precedence alias in another pool among the pairs' winners and runner-ups, named beside it (`picks.fallback`; zheref/nen#389).

## Worked examples

Domain, primary, the verb's runner-up, effort and restart line are checked against `nen direct resolve` by `--verify`; the recommended column and the aggregate fallback are this page's reading of `picks.recommended` and `picks.fallback`, which the verb does not compute yet (zheref/nen#389).

## Surfaces, restart lines and interactive equivalents

The actionable recommendation is always one of Hatsu's 4 surfaces. `direct` fills `<alias>` from `models` and `<level>` from the effort map — never a version.

| Surface | Restart line | Effort control | Model lookup | Interactive twin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Claude Code** | `claude --model <alias> (then /effort <level>)` | /effort low\|medium\|high\|max | the harness's model picker (/model) lists the served aliases | the Claude desktop app or claude.ai, the same model family |
| **Codex** | `codex -m <alias> -c model_reasoning_effort=<level>` | model_reasoning_effort low\|medium\|high\|xhigh\|max (ultra, automatic task delegation, exists and is never recommended) | codex debug models (slugs, default_reasoning_level and supported_reasoning_levels per slug) | ChatGPT's Codex web app or the Codex IDE extension, the same model family |
| **Cursor** | `cursor-agent --model <alias> (the alias is resolved to its served id first, docs/surfaces/cursor.md section 1; the id carries the dial as its suffix, -<level>)` | the model id suffix: -low\|-medium\|-high\|-xhigh (a -fast variant is a speed tier, not an effort) | cursor-agent models lists the served ids with their effort suffixes | the Cursor IDE chat and Composer, the same model |
| **Antigravity** | `the Antigravity workspace with Model: <alias> on the lead` | the model's thinking budget (pro) -- no four-step dial | the workspace's model picker | the Antigravity IDE itself, or the Gemini app for a conversation |

Surfaces `direct` knows of and never recommends as actionable (`surfaces.$nonActionable`): Surfaces direct knows of but never recommends as actionable: no docs/surfaces/<s>.md guide, no SurfaceRow in nen surface mirror, no hooks, picker or permission pack. Each appears as an INTERACTIVE equivalent where a cell names it. Adding one is a surface proposal through great-hiker (zheref/hatsu#236 for Grok Build), never a registry edit.

| Surface | Provider | What it is | Lookup |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Grok Build** (`grok-build`) | xai | xAI's agentic coding CLI: early beta 2026-05-14, v1.0 on 2026-08-07 under Apache 2.0, a SuperGrok or X Premium+ subscription; defaults to the Grok line, with an interactive TUI, a headless mode and ACP for editors | https://docs.x.ai/docs/models |
| **GitHub Copilot** (`copilot`) | github | the IDE chat and the coding agent; offers the Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok lines where the plan allows (Grok 4.7, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 listed GA on 2026-10-05) | https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/ai-models/supported-models |

Native IDE equivalents by language (offered beside the winner as the *interactive* row):

| Language | Native interactive option |
|---|---|
| Swift | Xcode's native integration (Apple Intelligence; ChatGPT and Claude where Xcode offers them) |
| Kotlin | Android Studio / IntelliJ (Gemini in Android Studio; Copilot where enabled) |
| TypeScript | VS Code or WebStorm with GitHub Copilot Chat, or the Cursor IDE |
| C# | Visual Studio with GitHub Copilot (Opus, Sonnet and Sol where the plan offers them) |
| Prose | the Claude desktop app or claude.ai |

## Where the version comes from

At run time `direct` reads the newest version of each pick's family and the effort dial its surface offers — the surface's own lookup first, then the provider's model page, quoted with its URL and date. Only when neither can be read does it quote the snapshot above, **with its date (2026-10-05)**, and the effort map's dial.

| Provider | Surface lookup | Effort dial, read live | Model pages |
|---|---|---|---|
| anthropic | the Claude Code model picker (/model), read in-session | /effort lists low\|medium\|high\|max in-session; the models page gives each model's default effort | https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview<br>https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview<br>https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing |
| openai | codex debug models | codex debug models -> supported_reasoning_levels per slug (low\|medium\|high\|xhigh\|max\|ultra on 2026-10-05) | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog<br>https://openai.com/index/practical-guide-building-gpt-6/<br>https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing |
| google | — | no dial | https://antigravity.google/docs/subagents<br>https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models<br>https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing |
| cursor | cursor-agent models | the -<level> suffixes cursor-agent models lists for the served id (grok-4.7-low\|medium\|high\|xhigh on 2026-10-05) | https://cursor.com/docs/models<br>https://docs.x.ai/docs/models<br>https://cursor.com/changelog<br>https://cursor.com/composer |

## Keeping this page true

```bash
bash scripts/direct_matrix_doc.sh --write      # re-render after any registry, taxonomy or models edit
bash scripts/direct_matrix_doc.sh --check      # exit 1 when this page is stale (lane direct-matrix-guard)
bash scripts/direct_matrix_doc.sh --verify     # every printed cell, level and example against nen direct resolve
bash scripts/direct_matrix_doc.sh --self-test  # the guard's own fixtures, then --check
```

Agreement with the verb is proved when `--verify` runs; staleness is caught when the lane runs. Neither runs on its own in CI yet (zheref/hatsu#234). A routing change is a registry edit through a PR, never an edit here; changing what an alias **means** is a maintainer ruling ([`ROSTER.md`](ROSTER.md) § *Rulings of 2026-10-04 — classify and direct*).
